test_title: PYST 14: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 16th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: general
question:
**Consider the following statements: **

1. The Concurrent List allows both Centre and States to legislate.

2. In case of conflict, State law prevails over Union law. Which of the above is/are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1 is correct:** The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution allows both the Centre and States to legislate on matters included in it. Examples include education, marriage, adoption, etc.
 
• The Concurrent List is one of the three lists under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, the others being the Union List and State List.
 
• Legislation on the Concurrent List ensures cooperation between the Centre and States while addressing shared responsibilities.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on the same subject, the **Union law prevails**, as provided under Article 254 of the Constitution of India.
 
• Thus, Statement 2 is incorrect because the Union law overrides State law in case of conflict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:**

 
 
• Subjects under the Union List are exclusively legislated by the Parliament.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, railways, and currency.
 
• It contains 97 subjects (originally) as per the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• Subjects under the State List are exclusively legislated by the State Legislatures.
 
• Examples include police, public health, agriculture, and local government.
 
• The State List originally contained 66 subjects.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• It contains subjects where both the Centre and States can legislate.
 
• It originally consisted of 47 subjects, which include criminal law, education, forests, and marriage.
 
• In case of conflict, Union law prevails as per Article 254 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 254:**
 
 
• If there is an inconsistency between laws made by the Parliament and laws made by State Legislatures on a Concurrent List subject, the law enacted by Parliament prevails.
 
• The only exception is if the State law has received Presidential assent, then it can prevail in that state.
